title: Disclosing pathogenic processes of monkeypox (MPOX) and drug repurposing through host-transcriptomics analysis.
authors: Mahmud, Sabkat; Ajadee, Alvira; Ali, Md Ahad; Ahmed, Md Feroj; Ahmmed, Reaz; Rana, Md Masud; Noor, Tasfia; Faysal, Md Fahim; Kabir, Md Hadiul; Mollah, Md Nurul Haque
one_liner_zh: 该文基于宿主转录组分析猴痘致病过程与药物重定位，虽含分子对接和MD模拟，但核心是药物-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Monkeypox (MPOX) virus infection outbreak in Africa in 2022 was initially considered a neglected tropical disease (NTD). Now it is recognized as a global health problem. The recent global spread has emphasized the need for increased attention to combat MPOX. Although there are some vaccines against MPOX, most people worldwide are still not vaccinated due to their unawareness or unavailability. However, so far, there is no approved drug against MPOX yet. Therefore, effective drugs against MPOX are also essential. This study attempted to disclose pathogenic processes and therapeutic strategies of MPOX based on MPOX-associated host key-genes (hKGs). At first, three transcriptomic profile datasets were analyzed, identifying 166 common host differentially expressed genes (hDEGs) between MPOX patients and control groups, comprising 75 upregulated and 91 downregulated hDEGs. Subsequently, six top-ranked host key genes (hKGs): ALB, HSP90AA1, CDH1, PTPRC, IGF1, and ABL1, were identified as potential MPOX-causing genes through protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis. Functional enrichment analysis of these hKGs revealed critical pathogenic processes of MPOX infection, including biological processes, molecular functions, cellular components, and KEGG pathways. Regulatory network analysis involving transcription factors and miRNAs provided further insights into disease mechanisms. Based on molecular docking analysis, five top-ranked drug molecules Tecovirimat, Beclabuvir, Maraviroc, Raltegravir, and Brincidofovir were identified as potential repurposable therapeutics against MPOX. ADME/T and drug-likeness evaluations confirmed favorable pharmacokinetic properties for these candidates. Additionally, 100 ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of the top three complexes (ALB-Tecovirimat, CDH1-Maraviroc, and PPARG-Beclabuvir) demonstrated strong binding stability, supported by RMSD, RMSF, and MM-GBSA results. Therefore, the results provided in this study might be potential resources for diagnosis and therapies of MPOX patients. However, the findings require experimental validation in wet lab for further confirmation.
abstract_zh: 2022年非洲猴痘（MPOX）病毒感染的爆发最初被视为一种被忽视的热带病（NTD）。如今，它已被公认为全球健康问题。近期的全球传播强调了加强关注以对抗MPOX的必要性。尽管已有一些针对MPOX的疫苗，但由于认知不足或不可及性，全球大多数人仍未接种疫苗。然而，迄今为止，尚无获批的针对MPOX的药物。因此，有效的抗MPOX药物也至关重要。本研究试图基于MPOX相关的宿主关键基因（hKGs）揭示MPOX的致病过程和治疗策略。首先，分析了三个转录组谱数据集，识别出MPOX患者与对照组之间166个常见的宿主差异表达基因（hDEGs），包括75个上调和91个下调的hDEGs。随后，通过蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（PPI）网络分析，确定了六个排名靠前的宿主关键基因（hKGs）：ALB、HSP90AA1、CDH1、PTPRC、IGF1和ABL1，作为潜在的MPOX致病基因。对这些hKGs的功能富集分析揭示了MPOX感染的关键致病过程，包括生物学过程、分子功能、细胞组分和KEGG通路。涉及转录因子和miRNA的调控网络分析进一步提供了疾病机制的见解。基于分子对接分析，确定了五种排名靠前的药物分子Tecovirimat、Beclabuvir、Maraviroc、Raltegravir和Brincidofovir作为潜在的抗MPOX可重定位治疗药物。ADME/T和药物相似性评估确认了这些候选药物具有良好的药代动力学特性。此外，对前三个复合物（ALB-Tecovirimat、CDH1-Maraviroc和PPARG-Beclabuvir）进行的100 ns分子动力学（MD）模拟显示了强结合稳定性，并通过RMSD、RMSF和MM-GBSA结果得到支持。因此，本研究提供的结果可能成为MPOX患者诊断和治疗的潜在资源。然而，这些发现需要在湿实验室中进行实验验证以进一步确认。
